AnalysisLens.description:
Six first-class TAM lenses (Q39).

Each lens has a structurally distinct math shape; frameworks are tagged to
exactly one lens and the framework picker filters by the concept's declared
lens. The validator enforces lens-tag agreement between concept and framework.
AnalysisLens.title: AnalysisLens

AnalystParaphraseSource.description:
Q40 paraphrase variant. ``snapshot_sha256`` is over the paraphrase +
metadata, not the original document — fair-use transformative.
AnalystParaphraseSource.title: AnalystParaphraseSource

AtomicPrimitive.description: One sourced number tied to a concept (Q2).
AtomicPrimitive.title: AtomicPrimitive

BannerKind.description:
Banner taxonomy. Surfaces in the UI (U10) and in PDF/markdown exports
as footnotes.

`analyst_paraphrase` covers Q40; `synthetic` and `modeled` cover Q20;
`subsidy` covers regime-modifier frameworks (e.g. IRA); `regulated` covers
Q36 clearance-gated outputs; `dark_estimate` flags low-confidence
primitives. `user_override` flags a transient what-if scalar the user typed
in the `/build` UI — never a sourced/persisted primitive (Strata Live).
BannerKind.title: BannerKind

CodeSystem.description:
Classification system a coded scope tag references.

``NAICS`` (industry) and ``SOC`` (occupation) are hierarchical and the guard
compares them by significant-prefix containment. ``CUSTOM`` carries a
human label with no machine hierarchy — the guard treats it as unverifiable
(``UNKNOWN``) unless two custom tags match exactly.
CodeSystem.title: CodeSystem

CodedTag.description:
One scope tag: a classification code plus a human label.

Multiple tags per dimension express a union — e.g. B2B sales reps as SOC
``41-3000`` (services) + ``41-4000`` (wholesale & manufacturing).
CodedTag.title: CodedTag

CompositePrimitive.description: Same-unit set op over atomic primitives (Q3).
CompositePrimitive.title: CompositePrimitive

Concept.description:
Default concept record. ``Marketplace`` and ``Company`` variants extend
this with extra mandatory fields (Q19, Q21) — out of scope for the v0.2
lens-aware slice but the schema leaves room.
Concept.title: Concept

ConceptAnalysisLens.description:
Primary + optional secondary lens (Q39).

The validator warns when scenarios from the two lenses land within 30% of
each other (means secondary isn't doing strategic work).
ConceptAnalysisLens.title: ConceptAnalysisLens

ConceptModifiers.description:
Four composable modifiers (Q39).

Each modifier is a field, not a separate lens; they layer onto whichever
primary lens the concept declares.
ConceptModifiers.title: ConceptModifiers

Convergence.description:
Bottoms-up vs tops-down cross-check (MV2). When a concept is sized by ≥2
*independent* method families, the two family medians are compared head to
head: the agreement ratio (high/low) is the triangulation signal a VC would
otherwise assemble by hand. This is pure synthesis of already-sourced
scenario values — no new number is invented. ``None`` (the default) means the
concept has a single method family, so there is nothing to converge and the
UI must NOT manufacture a second method.
Convergence.title: Convergence

ErrorDetail.description: The envelope FastAPI returns for an ``HTTPException``: ``{"detail": "..."}``.
ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail

FirmSizeBand.description:
A firm-size segment, e.g. mid-market = 100-999 employees.

``None`` on either bound means open-ended (``min_emp=None`` → from 0;
``max_emp=None`` → no upper limit). An all-firms scope is the absence of a
band (``segment=None`` on the scope), not a band with both bounds open.
FirmSizeBand.title: FirmSizeBand

FrameworkVariant.description:
Q17 declared variant. v0.2 uses ``scope`` to bind the framework to a
concept; sector/region variants land at later milestones.
FrameworkVariant.title: FrameworkVariant

InputRole.description:
Q6 input roles. Distinct from Q39 lens role names: a framework input
has both a ``name`` (matching a Q39 lens role like ``persona_pool``) and
a ``role`` (the Q6 time-travel role like ``base_value``).
InputRole.title: InputRole

InputScope.description:
The snap-to-truth scope of one consumed primitive, plus any divergences
from the concept's declared scope.
InputScope.title: InputScope

InputUsed.description:
One row of `inputs_used` on a scenario. Pinned by snapshot_sha256
(Q5) so the scenario is reproducible.
InputUsed.title: InputUsed

MarketScope.description:
The structured definition of a market (sub-project 1 design).

Every field defaults empty so an unscoped record is valid; the guard treats
an empty dimension as "unconstrained" on that side.
MarketScope.title: MarketScope

MethodFamily.description:
Q7 method families. Independence scoring warns when triangulation
uses two frameworks from the same family.
MethodFamily.title: MethodFamily

ScopeDimension.description:
The dimension a guard warning refers to (for UI grouping).

``VERTICAL``, ``PERSONA``, ``SEGMENT`` and ``GEO`` are code/range-anchored and
the guard emits warnings for them. ``PRODUCT`` (and the free-text
``include`` / ``exclude`` rules) are display-only in v1 — the guard never
emits a ``PRODUCT`` warning yet, because comparing free-text product
taxonomies is deferred to a later milestone. It is enumerated here so the UI
can group the product scope chips it renders.
ScopeDimension.title: ScopeDimension

ScopeReport.description:
Per-build scope check: the declared market scope plus, for each consumed
primitive, its true (displayed) scope and any mismatch warnings. ``ok`` is
True when no input diverged from the declared market.
ScopeReport.title: ScopeReport

ScopeWarningOut.description: One surfaced scope divergence on a consumed primitive.
ScopeWarningOut.title: ScopeWarningOut

TAMTrajectory.description:
TAM-over-time series derived from primitive ``as_of`` dates.

Each point represents the evaluator output at a distinct ``as_of``
date — using only the primitives available at or before that date. Points
where no framework is fully satisfiable are omitted; ``points: []`` means
the concept has no resolvable history at all.
TAMTrajectory.title: TAMTrajectory

TrajectoryPoint.description:
One data point in a TAM-over-time trajectory.

`value` is the triangulated midpoint of all satisfiable scenarios at this
snapshot date; `low`/`high` are the min/max of those scenario values.
TrajectoryPoint.title: TrajectoryPoint

Unit.title: Unit

info.description:
Proprietary curated market-sizing engine for VCs and operators.

**Data bank:** 307 atomic primitives from BLS, FRED, Census, EDGAR, and World Bank. All SHA256-pinned to source snapshots.

**Six TAM lenses:** cost_efficiency, revenue_generation, latent_demand, platform_throughput, bundle_consolidation, productivity_uplift.

**Dynamic resolution:** POST /resolve accepts natural language market queries, parses them into lens + primitives via Claude, searches for data via Exa, and streams results via SSE.
